“There is no zakāh on less than five awāq (of silver).”
“No zakāh is due on wealth until a year has passed over it.”
“On silver (money), one quarter of a tenth.”
“There is no zakāh on fewer than five camels.” And in the Book of Ṣadaqah: for five, a sheep; for ten, two sheep; for fifteen, three; for twenty, four; for twenty-five, a bint makhāḍ…
The Prophet ﷺ told Muʿādh to take “for every thirty cattle a one-year-old calf, and for every forty a two-year-old.”
“For forty sheep, one sheep… above one hundred and twenty, two… above two hundred, three.”
They must graze freely most of the year, be held a full year, and not be working animals.
“What is watered by the sky and springs, or by itself: a tenth; what is watered by irrigation: half a tenth.” And “there is no zakāh on less than five awsuq.”
“The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to pay zakāh on what we prepare for sale.”
“The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made Zakāt al-Fiṭr obligatory: a ṣāʿ of dates or a ṣāʿ of barley, on the slave and the free, male and female.”
“Zakāh is only for the poor, the needy, those who collect it, those whose hearts are to be reconciled, freeing captives, those in debt, in the cause of Allah, and the traveller.”
Scholars differ: the Ḥanafīs make zakāh due on gold and silver jewellery even when worn; the majority (Mālikīs, Shāfiʿīs, Ḥanbalīs) do not, for permitted jewellery kept for wearing.
If your wealth drops below the niṣāb during the year, the year is broken; when it reaches the niṣāb again, a new year starts.
